title: kv-cache: compact spillover pages and improve eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: In production we continue to see tail OOMs and degraded throughput under medium-to-high context churn workloads. Root cause analysis points at spillover paging creating many small partially-filled pages which increases fragmentation and causes the eviction selector to prefer evicting hot but fragmented entries. This PR introduces two orthogonal improvements: 1) a compacting spillover page layout that reduces per-page overhead and enables in-place compaction; 2) improved eviction heuristics that prefer consolidating fragments and consider page fill-ratio and expected re-use when ranking eviction candidates.

High level changes: compact spillover pages with a compact header and slot bitmap, add an async background defragmenter that opportunistically compacts under low-CPU utilization, extend eviction scoring to include page_fill_ratio and last_accessed_distribution, add a fast-path for continuous-batcher affinity to pin frequently used KV shards to the same worker to reduce cross-shard churn.

What I changed (summary): implemented compact spillover page allocator and on-page compaction routines in src/runtime/kv_cache_spillover.cc; added eviction scoring function and configuration knobs in src/runtime/kv_eviction_policy.h/.cc; introduced background defragmenter worker and runtime config in src/runtime/defrag_worker.cc; added unit and integration tests in tests/kv_cache_eviction_test.cc and tests/kv_cache_fragmentation_integration.cc; benchmark harness updates in bench/kv_cache_fragmentation_bench.py to reproduce fragmentation patterns; added docs describing runtime flags and operational guidance in docs/kv-cache-ops.md.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for new allocator and compaction logic - [x] Integration test that simulates continuous batching churn and verifies reduced page count - [x] Benchmarks show median tail memory usage down ~28% and p99 latency improvement in high-churn scenario - [x] Config defaults tuned to be conservative for existing deployments - [x] Added runtime knobs and observability metrics (page_fill_ratio, defrag_ops, compaction_bytes_saved).

Compatibility and rollout: This is backwards-compatible at the wire level; spillover pages are an internal on-disk/in-memory structure. Default behavior is conservative: background defrag is disabled by default and new eviction scoring is additive (does not change eviction target selection without opt-in via runtime flag). We plan a gradual rollout: lab -> canary -> region-by-region.

Testing and bench results: Microbench: run on a 8-GPU dedicated pool with synthetic churn workload (random context lengths, repeated prefixes). Results: peak resident set -28%, p99 response tokens latency -6% under sustained churn, eviction count per minute down 32%. CI: all unit/integration tests passed on linux-gnu pipeline, e2e bench job passed on canary hardware.

Related: Builds on prior work in ENG-4721/ENG-4810 and addresses incidents SUP-2214. See docs/kv-cache-ops.md for operator flags (runtime.defrag.enabled, runtime.eviction.fill_weight).

Notes for reviewers: focus on correctness of compaction (concurrent access), the eviction score math, and potential perf impact of background thread. I kept the background defrag opt-in and conservative by default; if we decide to enable by default we should run a wider canary first.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Great direction. Two asks: (1) show correctness under concurrent reader/writer access (add a stress test) and (2) consider a fail-safe counter to avoid long compaction pauses.

Aisha Patel (author): Added a stress test that runs mixed read/write/evict workloads and verified no assert failures. Compaction uses a bounded iteration with incremental progress to avoid long pauses; documented in comments.
Liam Chen: Can we expose a defrag throttle metric and a per-shard opt-out? Also please re-run bench on p3dn to validate cross-hardware impact.
Aisha Patel (author): Added runtime.defrag.throttle and runtime.defrag.per_shard_opt_out flags, and re-ran bench on canary p3dn-equivalent nodes; numbers included above.
Monica Ruiz: Security note: ensure compaction path doesn't leave stale pointers; added a quick review comment about sanitizer builds.
Aisha Patel (author): Verified with ASAN build in CI and added additional nulling paths to avoid use-after-free risk.
Diego Morales: Approved after seeing the stress test and bench numbers.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory efficiency by compacting spillover pages and adding improved eviction heuristics that reduce fragmentation and tail memory usage. Background defragmentation is opt-in and off by default. Operators can tune runtime.defrag and runtime.eviction.fill_weight.
notes_for_ops: Default config is conservative. To enable background defrag set runtime.defrag.enabled=true. Monitor metrics: runtime.kv.page_fill_ratio, runtime.kv.defrag_ops, runtime.kv.compaction_bytes_saved. Rollout recommended: lab -> canary -> canary-region -> global.
